newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn closes up despite options-related sale.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn closes up despite options-related sale.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed firmer in the nearby months on a reversal of spreads with the gains occurring despite significant bearish input from the corn options pit, traders said.
"It's just taking a breather, really quiet and is recovering a little," a trader said.
Corn dropped Tuesday on a slide in wheat futures and on overall good crop weather in South American growing regions.
Smith Barney bought 2,000 March $2.80 puts and bought 2,100 December $2.80 puts, which was viewed as a bearish stance, the traders said.
Traders were waiting for Thursday's USDA weekly export sales report with some pointing to a slight hike in farmer selling as helping to cap gains on corn prices.
Cash dealers early Wednesday said the expiration of some 30-day free storage agreements was prompting some farmer selling.
Trade estimates for Thursday's USDA weekly export sales report for corn were in a wide range from 500,000 to 900,000 tonnes.
Corn closed one cent a bushel higher to 1-1/2 lower, with December up one at $2.66.
Corn futures volume was estimated at 58,000 contracts, below the 84,841 traded Tuesday, according to the CBOT.

In corn options, in addition to the Smith Barney play, Goldenberg Hehmeyer sold 400 March $2.80 puts at 19-1/2 cents, FIMAT Futures bought 400 March $2.50 puts at 3-1/4 cents and bought 400 March $2.60 puts at 6-3/4 cents, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 20,000 contracts, below the 23,056 traded Tuesday.
